title: Knights of Doom!
reviewNotes: Three branches, 14 exact positions beginning after ...Kc1 at 107 seconds (seven pieces); earlier eight-piece setup and first underpromotion remain context. Rook sacrifice Rc2+ Nxc2, Nb3+, Kf1 and Kf2 force winning mating net. Three actual mates checked. Saved stable final image resolves captioned ...Nc3 to ...Nca3 from c2; b1 knight stays to defend c3.
transcript: Fools will resign because black is only two steps away from gaining a new queen, but white has a brilliant idea that starts with knight to C5, now attacking the pawn. So, if black doesn't want to lose it, he has to play pawn to B2, but white can follow through with his initial idea and play knight to B3 check, now forcing king to B1. Black is about to promote on the next move, but here is the idea, knight to D5, the other knight jumps in and now if you do get a queen after knight to B4, there is no way of preventing rook to D1 with a checkmate. And if you push the pawn, knight to C3 is going to be a checkmate. So, it seems like white successfully trapped the black king and the black is soon going to lose. But black does have one last trick up his sleeve, to promote the pawn, but to a knight, a brilliant under-promotion that stops both checkmate threats. If you play knight to B4, now you're just going to drop this knight and after this check, the knight is going to come back and defend the checkmate. But if you try to jump in with knight to C3, of course now the pawn has not moved, so you're just going to lose the knight. So, white decides to retreat and plays knight to D4, now collecting another pawn, but there is still an issue. If black manages to move the king and promote to a queen, black is actually still going to be winning. So, the black king can either move to A2 or to C1. Going to A2 would be a massive mistake. This knight has to stay where it is to prevent the checkmate. And this other knight doesn't really have any available squares that are not defended by one of white's knights.
